notes: Ordered fail-fast chain, gated on REAL process exit codes only — never scraped stdout, no `|| true`. A non-zero on ANY step fails QA and blocks the finish (verify-gate on Stop/SubagentStop).
1. cargo fmt --all --check: rustfmt in check mode across every crate in the workspace; exits non-zero on any unformatted file without rewriting it. Cheapest, broadest gate — runs first.

2. cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings: lint every target (lib, bins, tests, examples, benches) with all features on; `-D warnings` promotes ALL warnings (clippy + rustc) to hard errors so nothing merges dirty. Clippy also type-checks, so this doubles as the fast compile-error gate before the full build.

3. cargo build --all-targets: the authoritative compile of every target — proves the crate and its test/example/bench targets actually build, catching errors clippy's analysis-only pass can skip (link errors, build scripts, proc-macro expansion, cfg-gated code).

4. cargo test --all-targets: runs unit, integration, and doc-adjacent tests. `--all-targets` runs lib/bin/test/example targets; it does NOT run doctests — keep doctests green via a plain `cargo test` locally, but the gate standardizes on --all-targets for deterministic target selection.
Order is load-bearing: format and lint (cheap, broad) first, then the full build, then tests against that build.
`.format` is invoked by the format-on-save hook with the changed file path appended as the final argument (rustfmt --edition 2021 <file>); rustfmt formats the file in place.
This chain is written by /quetrex-init into <repo>/.quetrex/verify.json; the ENGINE's verify-gate reads .verify[] verbatim and eval's each command string in the repo root.
